seo.meta_title: 놀아 주다 Meaning | 'Play With' or 'Take You On'? From A2O LITE's NEON
seo.meta_description: AI translates 놀아 줄게 as 'I'll hang out with you'. 놀아 주다 is what adults do for kids — so between equals it can sound teasing or cocky.

ai_failure.situation: Your Korean coworker says 주말에 조카랑 놀아 줘야 해요, and later a friend jokes 내가 놀아 줄게. You ask AI about both.
ai_failure.ai_mistake: Translates both as 'hang out with', missing the -아/어 주다 that changes who is doing whom a favor.
ai_failure.why_it_fails: 놀다 is to play or hang out; adding 주다 makes it a favor. 놀아 주다 is what a parent or older relative does for a child. Between equals, 내가 놀아 줄게 can sound playful-cocky: 'I'll take you on' or 'I'll humor you'. The phrase appears in A2O LITE's 2026 debut song NEON.

natural_solution.rule: With kids and pets: 놀아 주다 is warm. With adults: say 같이 놀자 for 'let's hang out'; 놀아 줄게 sounds like you're doing them a favor.

alternatives.context: 'I have to play with my nephew this weekend' — adult with a child
'Let's hang out this weekend!' — the normal invitation between friends
'Play with me' — what a child says, or an adult whining jokingly

nuance: This is the same -아/어 주다 that turns verbs into favors: 들어 주다 (grant a request), 봐 주다 (let it slide). Who gives the favor matters, so the same verb can sound kind, needy or cocky depending on who says it to whom.
